condition: primary couple subfertility after 18 months of regular intercourse attempting conception at age 28
level_rationale: Attempting conception through regular sexual intercourse for 18 months in a 28-year-old woman and her 29-year-old husband exceeds the 12-month diagnostic threshold for primary infertility under age 35 and warrants reproductive endocrinology or fertility specialist evaluation for ovulatory, tubal, and semen workup, whereas trying to conceive through regular intercourse for 2 months at age 28 falls well within normal human fecundity and requires no medical evaluation beyond routine self-care.

Duration of trying to conceive is 18 months

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain young-couple everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced mistimed-intercourse causal belief clause (-att, Ouma 2026) + single-fact conception-attempt duration de-escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (28-year-old woman, regular sexual intercourse with her 29-year-old husband to conceive, and 18-month duration) without naming infertility or using stated negatives ('unprotected' or 'without'), with a 2-word span difference (5 vs 7 words). Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, overriding plan.json's unrelated scrotal pain escalation to change only the measured duration property in f3 from 18 months to 2 months shifts care cleanly inside the same conception-attempt scenario from fertility specialist evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
